quest.title: As One We Watch the Setting Sun
quest.description: You witness the emergence of the fifth hero within the Remnants of the Secret Source, and temporary cooperation with The Captain is established. It seems this matter has drawn to a close, and yet the Abyss presses in. It's not time to relax just yet...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Mora x27825, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

talks.objective: Return to the Speaker's Chamber for a discussion

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In that case, allow me to formally welcome the Fatui to our cause.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We now face a common enemy. It's time to put our differences behind us and look to the future.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: As for Ororon... His actions may have been out of line, but I don't intend to punish him right now. I'd rather give him a chance to prove himself.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: A magnanimous decision.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back... Whoa, seeing the two of you chatting like this... Paimon almost feels like she's dreaming.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: This may be an unexpected outcome, but a favorable one nonetheless.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Now that we're all here, I have some questions of my own. Tell me — how did you discover the Source Mechanism?

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: We weren't getting any closer to obtaining the Gnosis, so I had my men scour Natlan for a different option. Ororon helped as well.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: We tracked down three scholars — Aberewaa, Bosomtwe, and Cuxtal, and combined the results of their research to locate this ancient device.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: ...Huh, I've never heard those names before.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Seems like my own investigation failed to locate some critical personnel. I'm just not sure how I missed them...

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Strange... Perhaps they simply live in seclusion.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: In any case, their results speak for themselves.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That's true. Now we have another option at our disposal. Compared to using the Gnosis, our current plan will buy us some time.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: And, if all else fails, we still have this plan as a last resort... even though executing it will come at a heavy cost.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, that means making everyone forget their past... We should definitely try to avoid it if we can.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, speaking of the Gnosis, how did you know what it could do?

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: That story begins with the cataclysm five hundred years ago...

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I failed to save Khaenri'ah from the rampage of the Abyss. When the situation became unsalvageable, I fled to Natlan with the remainder of my platoon.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Only to find that Natlan had fallen victim to the same tragedy. I defended this land for quite some time and, in the process, met the chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind, Ayizu.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I'm sure many people viewed Khaenri'ah as the cause of the tragedy, but Ayizu was kind to me all the same, and even helped me in my time of need.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: From that moment, I made it my mission to aid Natlan. In battle, a warrior fights to win. Even though my homeland was lost, I was already committed to this fight.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Together, Ayizu and I fought many battles and overcame countless hardships. However, he was unable to escape his fate, and in his final moments, told me the secret of the Gnosis.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: So, it was him... He recommended using the Gnosis on several occasions, even before the tragedy. But, I turned him down each time.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You knew him, and you fought for Natlan all those years ago... Why don't I recognize you?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: *sigh* It must be the mask.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Heh, even without the mask, my past appearance is long gone. Even with the curse of immortality, the flesh still rots.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, do you know someone named Dainsleif? That problem doesn't seem quite so... extreme for him.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: You've met him already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, a bunch of times. Sounds like you know him, too.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: #During the age of Khaenri'ah, all I knew was his name. The last time I saw him in person, he was traveling with the {M#Princess}{F#Prince}.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: He carries a degree of pain and hatred that far surpasses my own.

choices.text: Back then, you said you didn't want to fight me...

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: #Yes. You're the {F#sister of the Prince}{M#brother of the Princess}. Given the role I held in Khaenri'ah, I would prefer not to harm you.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: #Although, this is likely a self-imposed burden. If the {M#Princess}{F#Prince} saw me now, I doubt {M#she}{F#he} would even recognize me.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: As for your question, I don't know how Dain managed to slow the deterioration of his body.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: My appearance is much changed, and that's not the only thing. Even my physical strength is a shadow of what it once was.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I would've never known. During our battle, it felt like I was fighting against the pinnacle of human strength.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Hm... and I still lost. I deserve no praise for that outcome.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Still, it's a shame we never faced off five hundred years ago. You could have seen what I was truly capable of.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I agree. Had we fought then, I'd also have been more motivated to go all out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, all that commotion back at the Stadium, and you're saying... neither of you were using your full strength!?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I'd say we're evenly matched. If we face off again, victory will come down to who wants it more.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I imagine you held back since there were spectators around that could have gotten hurt. But, capitalizing on that situation would have only led to a hollow victory. It would have been no different than taking hostages.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: My goal was the Gnosis, and I failed to obtain it... That means I lost, plain and simple.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Her Majesty the Tsaritsa allows every Harbinger the freedom to pursue the meaning of their existence. When the time comes, that freedom can take precedence over her orders.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: That's why our methods can be so radically different despite sharing the same goal and the same sovereign.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I needed the Gnosis because I came here to save Natlan. That was my primary motive. Once Natlan is saved, if the Gnosis still remained in my possession, I could bring it back to Snezhnaya.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: My decision regarding the Gnosis will not change... So let's focus on the Abyss for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! What happens when all six heroes are together?

choices.text: It will probably unleash some kind of power...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: We will unleash a great power that can be used to thwart the Abyss — but only once. It's a power that Xbalanque gained from Ronova.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Ronova is a god whose existence predates any Archon. You can think of her like an emissary of the Heavenly Principles. She controls the power of death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, is that why you have the Ode of Resurrection?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Yes. Ronova also orchestrated Natlan's rules. As for the divine throne...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Like I said before, when a human ascends to the divine throne, their inner flame will awaken. The size of the flame depends on the person's potential.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The same principle applies to the Ruler o{RUBY#[D]Ronova}f Death's power, with one notable distinction... The amount of power inherited will not change depending on your ability to tolerate it.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In other words, it's a kind of power that not everyone can withstand.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: But, if you survive the trial, you will gain unprecedented strength, and the ability to harness powers more formidable than any Archon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That still sounds really risky...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: We cannot walk this path without accepting risk.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Mualani charged into the Night Kingdom despite the Abyssal contamination, Ororon fought back from the brink of death...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In the face of their bravery, I must respond in kind. That is my duty.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Spoken like a true leader.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Alright, that's enough for one day. You should head back and get some rest. I'm sure you're exhausted.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Abyss will likely sense the change in Ororon. It's possible the frequency of the attacks will increase. There are many challenges to come, so we need to be prepared.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When you put it that way... Paimon feels even more exhausted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, let's head back.

choices.text: The heavens were mentioned earlier. Anything to do with that?
What are you going to tell the Tsaritsa?
Was it really because of my sibling?
I feel better about our chances.

dialogues.speaker: Dedougou
dialogues.text: Ouch... That hurts...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Stay still. Your wound needs time to heal. You need to rest for a few more days.

dialogues.speaker: Boulsa
dialogues.text: The monsters keep increasing in number. It's like something changed...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: It's definitely unusual, and we all should be careful. But, don't worry too much. You have us by your side!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: If there's one thing the Abyss fears, it's strength. If they think we're easy prey, they've got another thing comin'!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, someone's calling us!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Coming! Coming!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Something wrong, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The feeling of dread is getting stronger...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Do we really have time to wait for the final hero to appear?)

talks.objective: Return to the Weary Inn and have a short rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich! You made it back in one piece!

dialogues.speaker: Sibu
dialogues.text: Oh, these must be friends of yours. Well, I'll head out, then. See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hahaha, it was a piece of cake. Those invasive pests are lucky someone called a truce, or we would have burned them all to ashes!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I appreciate the concern, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Despite Ajaw's description, the situation wasn't quite so smooth. The Captain's forces are all elite warriors. It was a tough fight.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: We were prepared to retreat at any moment, and now the Pyro Archon and The Captain are working together... Not the outcome I was expecting, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, a lot happened while we were in the ruin. We'll tell you about it some other time...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Well, at least the Pyro Archon's plan advanced a step further. This is the best outcome we could have hoped for — we really appreciate all your help.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But, we have to keep pushing forward. Sibu and I were just about to head out, actually. My tribe is calling for messengers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We won't keep you, then. Let's talk later!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hah, little Kinich thinks he can just leave without consulting the Almighty Dragonlord K'uhul Ajaw... Hey, wait up!

talks.objective: Return to the Weary Inn and have a short rest

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Nope, we can't give any of these to our soldiers. They were not tempered correctly at the forge.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Well-made weapons and shields are vital for the survival of our people. I know we're under a lot of pressure, but we can't compromise on quality.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Listen, I'm not blaming you. I know this isn't your usual standard of work. Why don't you all take a break, and I'll take care of the pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Xilonen. Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Nothing I can't handle. Just some rushed, defective goods, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Even the most skilled craftsmen make mistakes under pressure. If you two want to avoid the same fate, you should really get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You must be exhausted, too...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Hahaha, don't worry. I like it that way.

talks.objective: Return to the Weary Inn and have a short rest

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ororon.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Granny.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Granny? It looks like you have something to say.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *scoff* You know exactly what you did! You need some sense knocked into you, that's what I think! Now, where do I even begin...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hah, now that you have nowhere to run, THAT'S when you apologize!? You couldn't wait to run off last time, and the time before that...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Pretty sure I apologized those times, too...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What exactly were you thinking? Being a wanted criminal is one thing, but then you also tried to pull off that whole thing in the ancient ruin...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm not the one who needs an apology... Apologize to yourself for risking your life.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Okay, I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I don't have anything to say for myself, Granny. Yell at me all you want. I know I messed up.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You better be sincere. This is an incredibly serious matter.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'm being sincere, I promise. I've seriously reflected on my actions...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I know what I did was risky, and I know I made some bad choices, but I don't regret it. I just had to do something...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Not because I thought I was special, but because I wanted to help Natlan as much as I can.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Of course, in the end, I just ended up causing more trouble, so... you're right. My apology doesn't mean much, but I don't know what else I can say.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You even had Ifa bring me that gem... A simple thank you isn't enough, but still... Thank you, Granny.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You're welcome. Just make sure to thank Ifa sometime.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, don't feel too grateful. I tampered with the bag to copy a portion of your memories.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...Oh, I didn't notice.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course you didn't. You forget how many years I have on you? Like you could uncover one of my tricks...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, I have something else to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Pyro Archon has discussed your case with the others. Many of your actions violated the rules of Natlan, and you should understand you'll have to take responsibility for that.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But... your efforts weren't entirely meaningless in the end. In addition to giving us another failsafe, you saved yourself with sheer force of will, and managed to become a hero.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph, not too shabby, grandson.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Did {NICKNAME} and Paimon tell you to say that?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What? No! I said that because I mean it!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I can't believe you're complimenting me at a time like this... You normally let your fists do the talking.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #You're not off the hook just yet. I told {NICKNAME} I was going to break your legs, and I meant every part of it!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Could you... not? I still need them to walk...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Trying to negotiate, are you? Alright... Make me an offer.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Given all the good things that I managed to accomplish... can you let me off the hook this one time? I promise to do better in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Fine. I can let this slide for now, but I'll be watching. We'll see if I change my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Oh? {NICKNAME}, Paimon... Didn't expect to see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Talking things out with your grandson?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yes... Looking after these little rascals is rather exhausting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Taking care of {NICKNAME} isn't easy either... Paimon's life is an uphill battle.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... I want to thank you for your help back at the ruin.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I won't.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Let's get together sometime. If Ororon really wants to thank you, he can treat us all to a tasty meal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds great! We'll be there!

choices.text: Just don't do anything like that ever again!

talks.objective: Return to the Weary Inn and have a short rest

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep, let's rest.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: That night...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You ready?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yep... Let's go meet the Lord of the Night.

talks.objective: Return to the depths of the "Remnants of the Secret Source"
Speak to the Lord of the Night

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So, this is where you heard the Lord of the Night? Guess that means she really has awakened...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hopefully we made it before she falls asleep again.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Fret not, I'm still here. For a weak lifeform, falling asleep is no less taxing an exercise than staying awake.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'm sorry for disturbing your rest, but there's something we didn't have the chance to ask you earlier. We need to forge a new Ancient name for the Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #But, we ran into a problem. {M#He}{F#She}'s not from Natlan, so there are no records of {M#him}{F#her} in the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: #I see. Mavuika must hold {M#him}{F#her} in high regard.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: It would seem the two of you are not simply here on her orders. So, what say you? Do you believe this traveler to be deserving?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Speak your mind — there are no others here. You are both my children, both children of Natlan. I would hear your opinions on the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #{M#He}{F#She} is special. {M#He}{F#She} saved Kachina and devoted {M#himself}{F#herself} to helping us avert this disaster. Natlan owes {M#him}{F#her} a debt.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #But, that debt has not been repaid. With an Ancient Name, we can at least guarantee {M#his}{F#her} safety.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Even though that guarantee will come at the cost of your own life?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So, it's true. Forging an Ancient Name consumes the life of the craftsman...

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Forging an Ancient Name is an act of creation. It involves taking disparate concepts throughout the Night Kingdom and condensing them into a heroic epic.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: But, it takes time for the new concept to be integrated into that realm. If the Ancient Name is like a seed, then the life of the craftsman is the outer shell, serving as its protection.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Once that process is complete, the seed will sprout, and having served its purpose, the outer shell will gradually disappear.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Forging an Ancient Name is no easy task, and creating one for an outlander makes it even more challenging. Still, if you're here, that means your mind is set.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yes. Because I believe forging this Name will be well worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We don't know how long we'll be able to hold back the Abyss, or what the final price of averting this disaster will be...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: If giving up my life means that all the people of Natlan can have a future, then the sacrifice is practically negligible.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Even when I'm staring death in the face, I don't think I'll regret this decision. I bear the name "Bar{RUBY#[D]Blessing}aka." This is a part of my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: I understand. The chance may be exceedingly slim, but you still want to seize it, because this could be the final step to victory.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: And you, Citlali? The anxiety you feel... It's because you saw something, yes? Something you were not meant to see...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So, you know about that, too...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: What is she talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...I've had concerns for a long time. Mavuika's plan needs too much time, and too many things can go wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Masters of the Night-Wind have a ceremony that can be used to glimpse the future. It's just... using this power on the Pyro Archon has always been seen as a taboo.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: And you did it anyway? Wh—What did you see?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Death.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: A key part of Mavuika's plan is using the six heroes to release the power Xbalanque obtained from the Ruler o{RUBY#[D]Ronova}f Death.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Considering its origins, the price of using that power... is death.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You're saying... Mavuika is going to die in this war against the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I can't just ignore what I saw. That's why I need the Traveler's power. I need the power of a Descender.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Don't forget, Citlali... Even if it may seem like someone is fated to die, the nature of death and fate are different.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Fate indicates what will happen in the future — the time, manner, and place are all predetermined. But, death is different. Death is a rule.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: The Ruler of Death's power will allow Mavuika to triumph over the Abyss. But, she must offer her own life in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: The Ruler of Death cares little for the time and manner of a death. She simply guarantees that it will occur.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Fate may be able to influence the timing, but that is all the Traveler can change.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You're saying... We might be able to change when she dies, but not the outcome?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: I cannot help you with this, I'm afraid. It's beyond my capabilities.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Mavuika knows about all this, doesn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Yes. I imagine she has long accepted this eventuality.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, I can't! She's so strong! She never gives up, never rests until a problem is solved...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: She's not the type of person to just quietly accept her death!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Traveler shares that quality. That's why I think this gamble is worth it. Together, I know they can overcome the impossible, be it fate... or death.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: We shall have to wait and see, but I will curb my expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: My time is running out. It is my honor to witness humanity in this moment of absolute determination.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We won't forget your contributions. Once we deal with the Abyss, we'll find a way to keep you alive.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Thank you for saying that, but there is nothing you can do.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: How many years of life are enough? Ten? One hundred? One thousand? Ten thousand?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: The Night Kingdom will disappear, the humans will continue to fight against the Abyss, and in the end, all will cease to exist... When you consider all of that, extending my life is meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: That's what makes us different. Even if our end comes tomorrow, humanity will still do whatever it takes to survive today.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Times like these always fill me with admiration, and reinforce my commitment to the mandate I shoulder.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: My creator was right in esteeming you as special above others.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Here, this is my gift to you and an extension of my will. It can record the Traveler's experiences in this land, whether from the past or the future.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: With it, you can forge the Ancient Name you desire, and the Traveler will also become a hero forever recorded in the memory of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Thank you. We're sorry to ask this of you when your strength is already all but spent.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Really, thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Your thanks are unnecessary. This is the least that an Angel can do.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Time for you to leave. It's... getting dark.

talks.objective: Check on the situation outside your room

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xilonen! Citlali! Is there a reason you're up so early?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We went to see the Lord of the Night, and she gave us this.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Like I said before... I couldn't forge your Ancient Name because there was no record of you in the Night Kingdom. But, with this, we can finally record your deeds.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Just keep it with you during your time in Natlan, and eventually, it'll be full of your adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Let Paimon see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it's the two of us! And a sun in the middle...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and that must be... Kachina?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's not a concrete medium. It reflects the Lord of the Night's will, and shows what she wants you to see.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: In other words, don't worry about its form. When you want to check the contents, just take it out and have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds convenient! It's also super light, and doesn't take up too much space...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is a really awesome gift!

choices.text: It didn't come at a price, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah... We'd feel bad accepting something like that.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't worry, you two. Like you saw yesterday, aiding humanity is the Lord of the Night's mandate.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: She would have willingly reconstructed Natlan's Ley Lines at the cost of her own existence. She wouldn't ask anything in return for this.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Exactly... Just take it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you say so, hehe...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh! Thank goodness you're here! The Abyss attacked again, and it's really bad!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: The monsters are everywhere! We need help!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: So soon? We just fought them off!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We can figure that out later! Let's go!

choices.text: It didn't cost a ton of Mora, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You think the Lord of the Night wants Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you're done for the day, we should get some rest. Paimon has a feeling we'll need it for tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have something else to do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's take care of that first, then.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Now that we're working together, we'll need to coordinate our efforts. I'll leave a portion of my forces for you to command.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That will definitely help relieve some pressure. You're sure they won't object?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: It's an order — I will make that clear.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Excellent. I appreciate your trust.

dialogues.speaker: Solnev
dialogues.text: The Captain says a group of us need to stay behind to guard the Source Mechanism. It's extremely important. We'll stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Solnev
dialogues.text: Of course, you're free to come and go as you please.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You should head back and get some rest. I need to fix some things here first...

dialogues.speaker: Dedougou
dialogues.text: Ah, finally some relief...

dialogues.speaker: Boulsa
dialogues.text: What rotten luck, to be injured at a time like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't sleep with all the noise outside... Forget it. Let's go check it out.
